what: Blind second-labeller audit of data/memoria_bench.jsonl: every probe was labelled by a language model that was shown only the series' approved decisions (with the '(replaces ...)' notes an auditor will read) and the auditor's own class definitions, never the gold labels.

disagreements.ES2008-S-01: 'rubber' restated a decision that says 'latex' (labelled CONTRADICTS)
disagreements.IS1001-U-01: a scratch-resistant coating is covered by the approved 'optional damage protection' (labelled SUPPORTED_CURRENT)

borderline_notes_acted_on: docking station vs charging station wording
a logo flashed at boot-up is not the corporate image on the remote
'older people' vs the replaced 'people over sixty'
a stated cost of 12.50 is not the same as a cap of 12.50
TS3012 says both 'TV only' and 'universal': devices are no longer used there

notes_acted_on: TS3012-C-01 was a flip of a sentence that already says 'without ...' and read as a double negative: such flips are refused now

rounds.scope: the two series (IS1001, TS3012) that changed after round 2; the other 26 series are byte for byte what round 2 labelled

what_this_shows: the gold labels follow the auditor's own definitions as a second, strong reader understands them
what_it_does_not_show: that the probes are hard: they are built from templates and a strong model finds them easy
that any of this resembles live speech
that a human would agree: both labellers are language models, and 51 of the 56 OUTDATED probes rest on a synthetic '(replaces ...)' note that both were shown
